filo   keeps a register of your files, where they live, and how long to keep them

Commands
  roots                    list roots and their settings
  roots add DIR [flags]    register a directory as a root, then scan it
  roots set DIR [flags]    replace a root's settings
  scan [DIR]               scan every root, or DIR inside a root
  report [--top N]         totals, files needing a retention, largest files,
                           duplicates, events
  export retention [DIR] -o FILE
                           write every file under DIR (or every root) with its
                           retention, as CSV
  export duplicates [DIR] -o FILE
                           write the duplicate groups with a copy under DIR, as
                           CSV
  update FILE [--dry-run]  record the retentions edited in an exported CSV
  delete [DIR] [-y]        delete the files past their retention, after asking
  delete FILE [-y]         carry out a duplicates CSV: delete the copies marked
                           delete, after asking
  duplicates               list what is not counted as duplicates
  duplicates exclude DIR   never count the files under DIR as duplicates
  duplicates include PATH  undo an exclusion, a content marked always or files
                           kept as separate files
  policies                 list the retention policies, and what needs attention
  policies add NAME [VALUE]
                           create a policy: a named retention such as bills = 7y
  policies set NAME VALUE  change a policy, and so every file using it
  policies move OLD NEW    move a policy's files to another, or rename it
  policies remove NAME     delete a policy no file uses
  policies show NAME       a policy's value and its files
  rules [DIR]              list the directory rules, at DIR and below
  rules add DIR [PATTERN] POLICY
                           give POLICY to the files under DIR with no retention,
                           now and as they arrive
  rules set DIR [PATTERN] POLICY
                           change the policy a rule gives new files
  rules remove DIR [PATTERN]
                           remove a rule; the files it set a policy on keep it
  rules move OLD NEW       move the rules at OLD and below it to NEW (a rename)
  rules copy OLD NEW       copy the rules at OLD and below it to NEW
  show PATH...             everything filo holds about a file or directory:
                           retention, history, copies
  set FILE... [flags]      set files' file_date, retention or duplicates
                           decision
  get FILE... --FIELD...   print fields of files, for scripts: --retention,
                           --keep-until …
  find [DIR] [flags]       list the files under DIR (or every root), by name:
                           --name '*bill*'
  help [COMMAND]           this overview, or a command's flags and rules

Every command accepts --db PATH (default: $FILO_DB, then the user data
directory).
Next: filo help COMMAND for a command's flags and rules
